headline_marked: [[GitHub Contribution Graph]] Not Showing Old Commits? It's Not a Bug, It's a Feature
headline: GitHub Contribution Graph Not Showing Old Commits? It's Not a Bug, It's a Feature
summary: Your past work might be invisible on your GitHub profile graph due to a disconnect between commit attribution and graph indexing. Here's why and how to fix it.
details: Many developers and engineering leaders rely on the GitHub contribution graph as a quick pulse check on activity. However, a common issue arises when historical commits, made with older, unassociated email addresses, fail to appear on the graph, even after the email is verified on the account.

The core of the problem lies in a distinction often overlooked: commit attribution and contribution graph indexing are separate systems. While adding and verifying an old email correctly attributes past commits to your profile, it doesn't automatically trigger a re-scan or rebuild of your historical contribution graph.

GitHub's system knows you authored the commit once attribution is fixed, but it doesn't automatically re-index your entire history for the visual graph. There's no public API or self-service button to force this historical rebuild; it requires manual intervention on GitHub's backend.

For engineering leaders, this is a data integrity issue that can impact assessments of team productivity and individual contributions. Relying on an incomplete graph can lead to unfair evaluations and invalidate metrics based on commit volume or frequency.

Before escalating, check if commits are on the default branch and if GitHub recognizes your email on individual commit pages. If these basic checks don't resolve the issue, the solution is to contact GitHub Support.

To get your historical contributions back on the graph, open a private ticket with GitHub Support. Provide the repository URL and an example commit SHA. Only GitHub staff have the necessary tools to manually rebuild your contribution graph.
